hypothesis: A fixed NVDA/AVGO diversification sleeve materially reduces NVIDIA concentration risk: monthly-rebalanced 50/50 NVDA/AVGO should improve Sharpe ratio while not worsening maximum drawdown or 95% Expected Shortfall versus NVDA-only, and should remain competitive after modest rebalance costs.

decision_rule.use_or_condition_if: 50/50 NVDA/AVGO must exceed NVDA-only Sharpe ratio without worsening maximum drawdown or 95% Expected Shortfall; cost sensitivity must not reverse the conclusion.
decision_rule.reject_if: 50/50 fails the Sharpe gate or worsens either maximum drawdown or 95% Expected Shortfall versus NVDA-only, especially in the more recent 2026 subperiod.

verdict_scope: Reject the claim that simply adding AVGO at a fixed 50% weight is a reliable risk-reduction substitute for NVDA concentration. This does not reject AVGO as a holding and does not test a point-in-time valuation-conditioned allocation rule.

market_data.price_type: unadjusted IEX monthly OHLCV close; real market bars, not synthetic fixtures

method.portfolio: 50% NVDA / 50% AVGO, reset to target weights monthly
method.expected_shortfall: historical 95% ES; with 19 monthly returns this equals the single worst observed month and is therefore a tail diagnostic, not a stable population estimate
method.transaction_cost: 5/10/20 bp multiplied by two-sided absolute rebalance-weight turnover at each month-end; initial purchase cost excluded equally from all allocation choices

primary_fundamental_context.context: Data Center revenue was $89.0 billion, up 117% year over year.
AI semiconductor revenue was $16.7 billion, up 221% year over year and 54% quarter over quarter.

interpretation.result: The diversification label is misleading here. NVDA and AVGO remained positively correlated (about 0.60 monthly), AVGO had substantially higher volatility, and the 50/50 portfolio worsened full-period Sharpe, maximum drawdown, and 95% Expected Shortfall versus NVDA-only. In 2026 Jan-Aug the deterioration was stronger.
interpretation.capital_allocation_decision: Do not reduce NVDA concentration by mechanically assigning a fixed 50% AVGO weight. Keep AVGO as a separately valued AI semiconductor candidate; any allocation shift should be justified by point-in-time expected return or a broader low-correlation sleeve, not by the assumption that two AI semiconductor names provide strong diversification.

risk_and_limitations: Monthly IEX closes are not verified total-return prices; dividends are omitted. This is a price-return allocation test, not an exact total-shareholder-return backtest.
Only 19 complete monthly returns are available in the selected recent period; 95% Expected Shortfall equals the worst month and must not be treated as a precise tail-distribution estimate.
Both securities share AI semiconductor and technology-cycle exposure, so the result does not generalize to diversification with bonds, gold, cash, or other lower-correlation assets.
No parameter fitting or look-ahead signal is used; this tests a fixed allocation, not the previously proposed point-in-time reverse-DCF selector.

implementation.reason: The fixed-diversification thesis was rejected. Retain only reusable negative evidence; do not add a production allocation model.

next_high_value_hypothesis: Using only information available at each quarterly rebalance date, does selecting or weighting NVDA versus AVGO by the lower reverse-DCF growth hurdle improve cost-adjusted out-of-sample return, maximum drawdown and Expected Shortfall versus NVDA-only and fixed 50/50?
